back: Work that harms a child's health, development or education because it is too heavy, long, dangerous or early.
Light, safe, age-appropriate tasks that leave time for school, rest and play.

front: Which section of the Constitution protects children from child labour?
What do ILO Conventions 138 and 182 do?
back: No. 138 (1973) sets minimum ages for work; No. 182 (1999) targets the worst forms of child labour.

front: When is World Day Against Child Labour?
Name four causes of child labour.
back: Poverty, school costs, orphanhood, demand for cheap labour (also attitudes, weak enforcement, disasters).

front: How does child labour create a cycle of poverty?
back: Children miss school, grow up with few skills, earn little as adults and may rely on their own children's labour.

front: Give four questions to tell child labour from a responsibility.
back: Is it suitable for the age? Does the child still attend school? How long does it take? Is it safe?
